gaps.sentence: He lost his job because of his ___ (HONESTY).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed — he lost his job
gaps.explanation: Losing a job implies wrongdoing, so the negative noun 'dishonesty' (dis- + honesty) is needed.

gaps.sentence: Her answer was ___ , so we had to ask again (RELEVANT).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — it did not relate to the question
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'relevant' is 'irrelevant' (ir- before r). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: The audience was ___ by her performance (CAPTIVE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ate forms the verb: captivate. The passive 'was ... by' needs the past participle 'captivated'.

gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.

gaps.sentence: There was a lot of ___ (OPPOSE) to the new road.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: opposition (-tion noun); 'opposite' is an adjective or noun meaning the contrary.

gaps.sentence: There has been a big ___ (IMPROVE) in her tennis.
gaps.explanation: After 'a big' a noun is needed: improvement (-ment noun).

gaps.sentence: This guidebook is really ___ for travellers (USE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ful means full of: useful. 'Useless' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.
